nodes.name: Spectral Sparsification Problem
nodes.statement: Given a weighted graph $G=(V,E,w)$ and $\epsilon>0$, produce a weighted subgraph $H=(V,\tilde{E},\tilde{w})$ with $|\tilde{E}|=O(n\log n/\epsilon^2)$ such that $(1-\epsilon)\sum_{uv\in E}(x(u)-x(v))^2 w_{uv}\le \sum_{uv\in \tilde{E}}(x(u)-x(v))^2\tilde{w}_{uv}\le(1+\epsilon)\sum_{uv\in E}(x(u)-x(v))^2 w_{uv}$ for all $x\in\R^V$.
nodes.statement_clean: Approximate a weighted graph by a sparse subgraph that preserves quadratic forms of the Laplacian to within a $(1\pm\epsilon)$ factor for all vectors.

nodes.name: Signed Edge-Vertex Incidence Matrix
nodes.statement: $B_{m\times n}$ defined by $B(e,v)=1$ if $v$ is $e$'s head, $-1$ if $v$ is $e$'s tail, $0$ otherwise. Then $L=B^TWB$ where $W(e,e)=w_e$.
nodes.statement_clean: The signed edge-vertex incidence matrix encodes edge orientations and yields the Laplacian as $L=B^TWB$.

nodes.name: Laplacian of a Weighted Graph
nodes.statement: $L=D-A$, where $A$ is the weighted adjacency matrix $(a_{ij})=w_{ij}$ and $D$ is the diagonal matrix $(d_{ii})=\sum_{j\ne i}w_{ij}$. Equivalently $x^TLx=\sum_{uv\in E}(x(u)-x(v))^2 w_{uv}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The graph Laplacian is the difference of the degree matrix and the weighted adjacency matrix.

nodes.name: Moore-Penrose Pseudoinverse of $L$
nodes.statement: $L^{+}=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{1}{\lambda_i}u_i u_i^T$, where $\lambda_i, u_i$ are nonzero eigenvalues and corresponding eigenvectors of $L$. Then $LL^{+}=L^{+}L$ is the projection onto $\mathrm{span}(\mathbf{1})^{\perp}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of the Laplacian inverts on the non-kernel eigenspace.

nodes.name: Effective Resistance
nodes.statement: The effective resistance $R_{uv}$ between vertices $u,v$ is the potential difference induced when a unit current is injected at one and extracted at the other; equivalently $R_{uv}=(\chi_u-\chi_v)^T L^{+}(\chi_u-\chi_v)$, and across an edge $e$, $R_e=b_e L^{+} b_e^T$.
nodes.statement_clean: Effective resistance is the potential difference under unit current flow; algebraically a quadratic form in the Laplacian pseudoinverse.

nodes.name: Projection Matrix $\Pi$
nodes.statement: $\Pi = W^{1/2} B L^{+} B^T W^{1/2}$. Diagonal entries are $\Pi(e,e)=w_e R_e$.
nodes.statement_clean: The matrix $\Pi$ encodes effective resistances on its diagonal and is the projection onto $W^{1/2}\mathbb{B}$.

nodes.name: Sampling-Outcome Diagonal Matrix $S$
nodes.statement: $S(e,e)=\tilde{w}_e/w_e=(\#\text{ of times $e$ is sampled})/(qp_e)$, so that $\tilde{L}=B^TW^{1/2}SW^{1/2}B$ and $\E S=I$, $\E\tilde{L}=L$.
nodes.statement_clean: The random diagonal matrix $S$ encodes how often each edge is sampled by Sparsify, with $\E S=I$.

nodes.name: Sparsify
nodes.statement: Randomized sampling algorithm that builds $H$ by drawing $q$ independent edges of $G$ with probability $p_e\propto w_e R_e$ and assigning weight $w_e/(q p_e)$ to each chosen edge.
output: Sparsifier Laplacian $\tilde{L}$ approximating $L$ in quadratic form

nodes.name: Approximate-Effective-Resistance Construction (build $\widetilde{Z}$)
nodes.statement: Builds a $(24\log n/\epsilon^2)\times n$ matrix $\widetilde{Z}$ via Johnson-Lindenstrauss projection composed with $W^{1/2}BL^{+}$, computed approximately by repeated linear-system solves.
output: Allows $O(\log n/\epsilon^2)$-time queries of approximate effective resistance

nodes.name: Sample JL projection matrix $Q$
nodes.statement: Let $Q$ be a random $\pm 1/\sqrt{k}$ matrix of dimension $k\times n$ with $k=24\log n/\epsilon^2$.

nodes.name: Compute $Y=QW^{1/2}B$
nodes.statement: Multiply $Q$ by $W^{1/2}B$; takes $\widetilde{O}(m/\epsilon^2)$ time since $B$ has $2m$ entries and $W^{1/2}$ is diagonal.

nodes.name: Solve for each row using STSolve
nodes.statement: For each row $y_i$ of $Y$ ($1\le i\le k$), compute $\tilde{z}_i=\mathtt{STSolve}(L,y_i,\delta)$ with $\delta=\frac{\epsilon}{3}\sqrt{\frac{2(1-\epsilon)w_{min}}{(1+\epsilon)n^3 w_{max}}}$; assemble rows into $\widetilde{Z}$.

nodes.name: Main Theorem (Spectral Sparsification by Effective Resistance)
nodes.statement: If $q=9C^2 n\log n/\epsilon^2$ where $C$ is the constant of Lemma \ref{lemrud}, and $n$ is sufficiently large, then with probability $\ge 1/2$, $\forall x\in\R^n$: $(1-\epsilon)x^TLx\le x^T\tilde{L}x\le (1+\epsilon)x^TLx$.

nodes.name: Fast Effective-Resistance Approximation
nodes.statement: There is an $\widetilde{O}(m(\log r)/\epsilon^2)$-time algorithm that, given $\epsilon>0$ and $G=(V,E,w)$ with $r=w_{max}/w_{min}$, computes a $(24\log n/\epsilon^2)\times n$ matrix $\widetilde{Z}$ such that with probability $\ge 1-1/n$: $(1-\epsilon)R_{uv}\le\|\widetilde{Z}(\chi_u-\chi_v)\|^2\le (1+\epsilon)R_{uv}$ for every $u,v\in V$.

nodes.name: Sparsifier with Bounded-Edge-Weight-Blowup Property
nodes.statement: There is an $\widetilde{O}(m/\epsilon^2)$-time algorithm which on input $G=(V,E,w),\epsilon>0$ produces $H=(V,\tilde{E},\tilde{w})$ with $O(n\log n/\epsilon^2)$ edges that, with probability $\ge 1/2$, satisfies both the spectral guarantee (\ref{xtlx}) and the bound $\sum_{e\ni v}\tilde{w}_e/w_e\le 2\deg(v)$ for all $v$.
conclusions: With probability $\ge 1/2$, $H$ satisfies both the spectral approximation and the per-vertex weight-blowup bound

nodes.name: Spielman-Teng Linear System Solver
nodes.statement: There is an algorithm $x=\mathtt{STSolve}(L,y,\delta)$ that, given a Laplacian $L$, vector $y$, and error parameter $\delta>0$, returns $x$ with $\|x-L^{+}y\|_L\le \delta\|L^{+}y\|_L$ in expected time $\widetilde{O}(m\log(1/\delta))$.
assumptions: $L$ a Laplacian matrix with $m$ nonzero entries

nodes.name: Projection Matrix Lemma
nodes.statement: (i) $\Pi$ is a projection matrix; (ii) $\im(\Pi)=\im(W^{1/2}B)=W^{1/2}\mathbb{B}$; (iii) eigenvalues of $\Pi$ are $1$ with multiplicity $n-1$ and $0$ with multiplicity $m-n+1$; (iv) $\Pi(e,e)=\|\Pi(\cdot,e)\|^2$.

nodes.name: Reduction to Spectral Approximation of $\Pi$
nodes.statement: If $S$ is nonnegative diagonal with $\|\Pi S\Pi - \Pi\Pi\|_2\le\epsilon$, then $\forall x\in\R^n$: $(1-\epsilon)x^TLx\le x^T\tilde{L}x\le (1+\epsilon)x^TLx$, where $L=B^TWB$ and $\tilde{L}=B^TW^{1/2}SW^{1/2}B$.

nodes.name: Rudelson-Vershynin Concentration Inequality
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{p}$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega\subseteq\R^d$ with $\sup_{y\in\Omega}\|y\|_2\le M$ and $\|\E_{\mathbf{p}}yy^T\|_2\le 1$. For independent samples $y_1,\ldots,y_q$: $\E\|\frac{1}{q}\sum_{i=1}^q y_iy_i^T-\E yy^T\|_2\le \min(CM\sqrt{\log q/q},1)$ for an absolute constant $C$.

nodes.name: Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma (Achlioptas form)
nodes.statement: Given fixed vectors $v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\R^d$ and $\epsilon>0$, let $Q_{k\times d}$ be a random $\pm 1/\sqrt{k}$ matrix with $k\ge 24\log n/\epsilon^2$. Then with probability $\ge 1-1/n$: $(1-\epsilon)\|v_i-v_j\|_2^2\le \|Qv_i-Qv_j\|_2^2\le (1+\epsilon)\|v_i-v_j\|_2^2$ for all $i,j\le n$.
conclusions: With probability $\ge 1-1/n$, all pairwise squared distances are preserved within factor $(1\pm\epsilon)$

nodes.name: STSolve-Error to Effective-Resistance-Error Bound
nodes.statement: If $(1-\epsilon)R_{uv}\le\|Z(\chi_u-\chi_v)\|^2\le (1+\epsilon)R_{uv}$ for all $u,v$, and $\|z_i-\tilde{z}_i\|_L\le\delta\|z_i\|_L$ for all $i$ with $\delta\le\frac{\epsilon}{3}\sqrt{\frac{2(1-\epsilon)w_{min}}{(1+\epsilon)n^3 w_{max}}}$, then $(1-\epsilon)^2 R_{uv}\le\|\widetilde{Z}(\chi_u-\chi_v)\|^2\le (1+\epsilon)^2 R_{uv}$ for every $uv$.
assumptions: $Z$ already a $(1\pm\epsilon)$-approximation of resistances on all pairs

nodes.name: Bounded Edge-Weight Blowup Lemma
nodes.statement: If we sample $q>4n\log n/\beta$ edges of $G$ in $\mathbf{Sparsify}$ with $p_{(u,v)}\ge\beta/(n\min(\deg(u),\deg(v)))$ for some $0<\beta<1$, then with probability $\ge 1-1/n$: $\sum_{e\ni v}\tilde{w}_e/w_e\le 2\deg(v)$ for all $v\in V$.
conclusions: With probability $\ge 1-1/n$, $\sum_{e\ni v}\tilde{w}_e/w_e\le 2\deg(v)$ for all $v\in V$

nodes.name: Sparsifier Robustness to Approximate Resistances
nodes.statement: If $Z_e\ge R_e/\alpha$ and $\sum_e w_eZ_e\le \alpha\sum_e w_eR_e$ for $\alpha\ge 1$, and we sample with $p_e'=w_eZ_e/\sum_e w_eZ_e$, then with probability $\ge 1/2$: $(1-\epsilon\alpha)x^T\tilde{L}x\le x^TLx\le(1+\epsilon\alpha)x^T\tilde{L}x$ for all $x\in\R^n$.

nodes.name: Lower Bound on Effective Resistance
nodes.statement: If $G=(V,E,w)$ is a connected graph, then for all $u,v\in V$: $R_{uv}\ge\frac{2}{n w_{max}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Projection Matrix Lemma
nodes.statement: Direct algebraic manipulation using $L=B^TWB$ and the identity $L^{+}L=$ projection onto $\im(L^{+})$, combined with rank counting.

nodes.name: Show $\Pi^2=\Pi$
nodes.statement: Expand $\Pi^2=W^{1/2}BL^{+}(B^TWB)L^{+}B^TW^{1/2}=W^{1/2}BL^{+}LL^{+}B^TW^{1/2}=\Pi$ using $L=B^TWB$ and $L^{+}L$ being the identity on $\im(L^{+})$.

nodes.name: Identify $\im(\Pi)$ with $\im(W^{1/2}B)$
nodes.statement: One inclusion follows from $\Pi=W^{1/2}B(\cdot)$. The reverse inclusion follows by taking $y=W^{1/2}Bx$ with $x\perp\ker(L)$ and computing $\Pi y=y$.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue counting
nodes.statement: Since $\dim\im(W^{1/2}B)=n-1$ and $\Pi^2=\Pi$, eigenvalues are $0/1$ with multiplicities $m-n+1$ and $n-1$. Part (iv) follows from symmetry.

nodes.name: Proof of Reduction Lemma
nodes.statement: Restrict the spectral-norm bound to $\im(W^{1/2}B)$ where $\Pi$ acts as identity, parametrize $y=W^{1/2}Bx$, and reduce to the Laplacian quadratic form.

nodes.name: Proof of Main Theorem
nodes.statement: Express $\Pi S\Pi$ as a sum of i.i.d. rank-1 outer products, apply Rudelson-Vershynin to bound the spectral norm of the deviation, then invoke Markov's inequality and Lemma LP472.2.

nodes.name: Identify sampling distribution
nodes.statement: Since $\sum_e w_e R_e=\mathrm{Tr}(\Pi)=n-1$ by Lemma \ref{lempi}.(iii), $p_e=w_eR_e/(n-1)$.

nodes.name: Rewrite $\Pi S\Pi$ as sum of rank-1 outer products
nodes.statement: $\Pi S\Pi=\frac{1}{q}\sum_{i=1}^q y_iy_i^T$ with $y=\Pi(\cdot,e)/\sqrt{p_e}$ drawn with probability $p_e$.

nodes.name: Bound moments of $y$
nodes.statement: $\E yy^T=\Pi$, so $\|\E yy^T\|_2=1$; norm bound $\|y\|_2=\sqrt{n-1}$ via $\Pi(e,e)=w_e R_e$.

nodes.name: Apply Rudelson-Vershynin
nodes.statement: With $q=9C^2 n\log n/\epsilon^2$, $\E\|\Pi S\Pi-\Pi\Pi\|_2\le \epsilon/2$ for $n$ large enough since $\epsilon\ge 1/\sqrt{n}$.

nodes.name: Markov + Lemma LP472.2
nodes.statement: By Markov's inequality, $\|\Pi S\Pi-\Pi\|_2\le\epsilon$ with probability $\ge 1/2$. Lemma LP472.2 then yields the spectral bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Sparsifier Robustness Corollary
nodes.statement: Show $p_e'\ge p_e/\alpha^2$ from the hypotheses and rerun the proof of TP472.1; the norm bound on $y$ acquires a factor $\alpha$, giving the $\epsilon\alpha$ guarantee.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP472.2
nodes.statement: Express $R_{uv}$ as $\|W^{1/2}BL^{+}(\chi_u-\chi_v)\|^2$, project via Johnson-Lindenstrauss, then approximate the projected vectors using STSolve and bound the propagated error via LP472.5.

nodes.name: Rewrite $R_{uv}$ as squared Euclidean distance
nodes.statement: $R_{uv}=\|W^{1/2}BL^{+}(\chi_u-\chi_v)\|_2^2$, so resistances become pairwise squared distances among $\{W^{1/2}BL^{+}\chi_v\}_{v\in V}$.

nodes.name: Apply Johnson-Lindenstrauss
nodes.statement: Project onto $k=24\log n/\epsilon^2$ random directions via $Q$; with probability $\ge 1-1/n$, all pairwise squared distances are preserved up to $(1\pm\epsilon)$.

nodes.name: Set $Z=QW^{1/2}BL^{+}$ and approximate by STSolve
nodes.statement: Compute each row $\tilde{z}_i=\mathtt{STSolve}(L,y_i,\delta)$ where $y_i$ are rows of $Y=QW^{1/2}B$.

nodes.name: Bound STSolve-induced error via Lemma LP472.5
nodes.statement: Choose $\delta=\frac{\epsilon}{3}\sqrt{\frac{2(1-\epsilon)w_{min}}{(1+\epsilon)n^3 w_{max}}}$ so that $\|\widetilde{Z}(\chi_u-\chi_v)\|^2\approx R_{uv}$ within $(1\pm\epsilon)^2$.

nodes.name: Total runtime $\widetilde{O}(m\log r/\epsilon^2)$
nodes.statement: $O(\log n/\epsilon^2)$ STSolve calls of cost $\widetilde{O}(m\log(1/\delta))=\widetilde{O}(m\log r)$ each.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP472.5
nodes.statement: Use the triangle inequality along a simple path $P$ from $u$ to $v$, Cauchy-Schwarz, the Frobenius-norm rewrite, and the lower bound $R_{uv}\ge 2/(nw_{max})$ from Proposition PrP472.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition PrP472.1
nodes.statement: By Rayleigh's monotonicity law, $R_{uv}\ge R_{uv}'$ for $G'=w_{max}\cdot K_n$. By symmetry, every $R_{uv}'=2/(nw_{max})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Bounded-Blowup Lemma
nodes.statement: Define i.i.d. variables $X_i$ with $\E X_i=\deg(v)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(X_i)\le n\deg(v)^2/\beta$. Apply Bennett's inequality with $q\ge 4n\log n/\beta$ to get failure probability $1/n^2$ per vertex; union bound.

nodes.name: Define i.i.d. random variables $X_i$
nodes.statement: $X_i=1/p_e$ if edge $e\ni v$ is the $i$th sampled edge, else $0$; then $D_v=\frac{1}{q}\sum_i X_i=\sum_{e\ni v}\tilde{w}_e/w_e$.

nodes.name: Compute moments of $X_i$
nodes.statement: $\E X_i=\deg(v)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(X_i)\le n\deg(v)^2/\beta$ via the assumed lower bound on $p_{(u,v)}$.

nodes.name: Apply Bennett's inequality
nodes.statement: $\P[D_v>2\deg(v)]\le\exp(-\beta q/(2n))\le 1/n^2$ once $q\ge 4n\log n/\beta$.

nodes.name: Union bound over vertices
nodes.statement: Take a union bound over all $n$ vertices to get probability $\ge 1-1/n$.

nodes.name: Spectral Sparsifier Quadratic-Form Guarantee
nodes.statement: $(1-\epsilon)\sum_{uv\in E}(x(u)-x(v))^2 w_{uv}\le \sum_{uv\in\tilde{E}}(x(u)-x(v))^2\tilde{w}_{uv}\le(1+\epsilon)\sum_{uv\in E}(x(u)-x(v))^2 w_{uv}$.

nodes.name: Ultrasparsifier Property
nodes.statement: $\sum_{e\ni v}\tilde{w}_e/w_e\le 2\deg(v)$ for every vertex $v\in V$.

nodes.name: Sampling Probability with Min-Degree Mixing
nodes.statement: $p'_e=p'_{(u,v)}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\|Zb_e^T\|^2 w_e}{\sum_e\|Zb_e^T\|^2 w_e}+\frac{1}{n\min(\deg(u),\deg(v))}\right)$.

nodes.name: Sparsifiers Approximately Preserve Effective Resistances
nodes.statement: Condition (\ref{xtlx}) implies $\frac{1}{1+\epsilon}x^TL^{+}x\le x^T\tilde{L}^{+}x\le\frac{1}{1-\epsilon}x^TL^{+}x$, so effective resistances $(\chi_u-\chi_v)^TL^{+}(\chi_u-\chi_v)$ are also approximately preserved by the sparsifier.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue Approximation via Courant-Fischer
nodes.statement: If $\lambda_i,\tilde{\lambda}_i$ are eigenvalues of $L$ and $\tilde{L}$, then $(1-\epsilon)\lambda_i\le\tilde{\lambda}_i\le(1+\epsilon)\lambda_i$ by Courant-Fischer; the same relation holds for the normalized Laplacian $D^{-1/2}LD^{-1/2}$ and the random-walk matrix $D^{-1}L$.
